subject: NUMVAL-F function
notes: RE-DETERMINED 2026-10-26 (kb/Work PB3839, owner: "We should always be consistent with ourself barring an explicit requirement differently"). §15.69.4 r2: under native (and standard-binary) arithmetic the returned value is an APPROXIMATION of the value represented by argument-1, and §15.4.1 leaves a native returned value's characteristics and representation to the implementor; r3 gives standard-decimal arithmetic the value itself. WiseOwl COBOL's determination (CONFORMANCE.md item 92) is that the approximation IS r3's value: the exact parse, significand × 10^(exponent − fraction digits), carried as an SDIDI (NumvalFDec) exactly as NUMVAL's is, in EVERY mode, channel and receiver (IntrinsicCarrierRules.ReturnsExactParse routes NUMVAL, NUMVAL-C and NUMVAL-F to RenderDec's one arm; NUMVAL-F has no RenderNum arm and no receiver test). A fixed-point receiver rounds it ONCE with the statement's own rule (§14.7.4.1, §14.7.4.3 rules 2-10) and a MOVE truncates it (§14.6.8.2 rule 4); a floating-point receiver converts the exact decimal once and lands it as it lands any decimal sender (a MOVE rounds to nearest, a COMPUTE with no ROUNDED phrase truncates, CONFORMANCE.md item 81); DISPLAY renders the item-92 text form of the exact value at its own scale and a relation compares exact values. The earlier determination (the float family's: a binary64 in a receiver-less or float-receiver context, an Int128 parse truncated at the receiver-capped max(scale, 9) for a fixed receiver) gave one reference several values and rounded a fixed-point receiver's value twice: ROUNDED MODE AWAY-FROM-ZERO of NUMVAL-F("0.12340000000001") into PIC 9V9(4) stored 0.1234 where NUMVAL and GnuCOBOL store 0.1235. A conforming native argument whose magnitude passes decimal128's range (NUMVAL-F("1E+7000")) is the size error condition of the implementor-defined intermediate range (§14.7.5 case 5, item 179), as it is for every SDIDI-carried native value. The binary64 and binary32 conversions of the NUMVAL-F text survive only for the ACCEPT device transfer into a floating-point receiver. The closed set of places IntrinsicRenderer reads its receiver is held by ReceiverShapeReaderDriftTests; MAX and MIN, the sibling that truncated the selected value at a coarser receiver's scale before its ROUNDED phrase ran, are fixed with it (pb3839_max_min_round_once).
